newsitem.title: JAPAN: SEC launches probe into Suzutan president - source.
newsitem.headline: SEC launches probe into Suzutan president - source.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission has begun a probe into alleged insider trading by Suzutan Co Ltd president Katsurao Suzui, a source close to the commission said on Monday.
An official at the securities watchdog declined to comment on details of the investigation.
A Suzutan official said the company plans to hold a news conference at 11.00 a.m. (0200 GMT) in Nagoya, where the company's headquarters are based.
Suzutan is a women's wear retailer and lists its shares on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

The NHK public television network reported on Monday that Suzui, then chairman of the company, sold one million shares of his company before the company announced a 6.6 billion yen loss in October 1994.
Following the loss announcement, shares in the company, which are listed on the first section of Tokyo Securities Exchange, plunged to around 900 yen from 1,300 yen, NHK reported.
